findings.claim: When a bad UTF-8 byte cuts off an oversized field, long-record recovery marks absent trailing columns as readable. Monzo can then refuse a fabricated empty Amount and omit the oversized-field diagnosis.
findings.repro: Use the Monzo header `Transaction ID,Date,Type,Currency,Name,Amount,Balance`. On line 2 write `tx_1,01/01/2026,Faster payment,GBP,` followed by 200,000 ASCII Ns, a raw byte 0xE9, then `,1.00,1.00` and a newline. Invoke `cma import monzo input.csv --out output.csv`. UTF-8 recovery passes the prefix ending in the oversized Name to the CSV reader. Long-record recovery pads Amount with an empty string and marks it readable, so Monzo reports `Amount '' is not a plain amount` instead of reporting that a field on line 2 is too long to read.
